items.title: Anthropic's Claude now writes code and proves it safe automatically
items.summary: Anthropic had Claude generate mathematical proofs that existing code is correct, producing roughly 180 million lines of proof code for 123 open-source libraries. Along the way, the model caught bugs that years of testing had missed. Anthropic's goal: making formal verification with AI as routine as standard testing. The article Anthropic's Claude now writes code and proves it safe automatically appeared first on The Decoder.

items.summary: OpenAI is closing in on a new funding round of up to $30 billion but has lowered its valuation target to get there. The article OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials
items.summary: Customers are letting AI agents use their credentials to access accounts at Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and other major U.S. banks, sometimes without direct instructions. Morgan Stanley has blocked agents, while other banks are restricting access. Most plan to limit agents to read-only access. The article Major US banks are locking out AI agents that log in with customer credentials appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Google's Agent Compute Engine gives every Gemini agent its own hardware-isolated micro virtual machine
items.summary: With Agent Compute Engine, Google is introducing a runtime environment designed specifically for AI agents, while also expanding the governance capabilities that enable companies to manage agents in cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments. The article Google's Agent Compute Engine gives every Gemini agent its own hardware-isolated micro virtual machine appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.summary: Only 13 percent of companies are getting real business value from their AI investments, according to a Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs. At the same time, 51 percent expect AI to actually increase their operating costs. Yet 75 percent of CEOs plan to keep raising their technology budgets. items.title: Recursive shows first result of its AI-driven research process with Flint
items.summary: The AI startup Recursive is unveiling Flint, its first language model, a 40-billion-parameter MoE for local coding developed by former DeepMind researchers. It was created in four months using the company's in-house AI system, "Eureka Machine," which independently tests and optimizes architectures. items.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.summary: Security researchers at Symantec have found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the web and uses them to attack servers, steal databases, and install cryptominers on its own. It runs up to 100,000 steps without human input. The owner of the hijacked model gets stuck with the bill. items.summary: OpenAI teamed up with PerturbAI and Scripps Research to deploy thousands of AI agents that analyzed biological data from millions of mouse cells. The article OpenAI agents analyze mouse brain data in 32 minutes, a job that would take humans months appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
items.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that handles tasks on its own, even when the user is offline. The app is built on Claude Opus 5.5 and connects to services like Gmail, Slack, and Stripe through more than 6,000 connectors. It asks for approval before sensitive actions like payments.
